messages:
kevin: Heads up — after the nightly perf run I see a 1.6GB per-rank memory bump on 8xA100 jobs. Suspect NCCL comm workspace is sizing badly when seq lengths are mixed (short+long).

maya: Ugh. Which workload? the chat-gen sweep?

kevin: Yeah, chat-gen v12 with dynamic batching. It only spikes when we have a few long seqs in the batch. Short-only batches look fine.

ara: Could be comm buffer = O(max_seq_len * tp_shard_factor) and we don't clamp by actual nonpad tokens. We saw similar with staging arenas earlier.

kevin: I grabbed a mem profile from last run:

perf-bot: snapshot from 2026-03-17 03:12 UTC
```
rank0: used=23.1G  comm_buf=1.2G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.5G
rank1: used=24.7G  comm_buf=1.6G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.4G
rank2: used=22.9G  comm_buf=1.0G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.3G
rank3: used=25.0G  comm_buf=1.7G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.6G
rank4: used=23.4G  comm_buf=1.1G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.4G
rank5: used=24.0G  comm_buf=1.5G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.5G
rank6: used=23.7G  comm_buf=1.3G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.4G
rank7: used=22.8G  comm_buf=1.2G  kv_cache=9.6G  temp=0.4G
```

maya: comm_buf variance is large across ranks. That implies NCCL workspace per-rank scaling depending on local tensor shapes.

ara: Also look at KV cache — it's constant across ranks which means per-shard duplicate copies are expected because we shard tensors but still allocate full KV per shard in current code path. That multiplies memory for TP=8.

dennis: Can you repro with MT-run but with disabled kv-copy optimization? Might prove duplicate clone is the culprit.

kevin: Ran a quick compare: with kv_clone_disabled=true the total per-GPU falls ~0.9G on average. So KV duplication accounts for a chunk but not all.

zach: So two knobs: 1) NCCL comm workspace sizing 2) KV cache replication strategy.

maya: For comm workspace, propose adaptive sizing: compute per-collective expected max payload as max_nonpad_tokens_in_batch * bytes_per_token_per_shard, clamp to a percentile (e.g. 95th) across recent windows, and allocate a shared comm-pool of N workspaces instead of ephemeral per-collective alloc. This reduces tail and reuse churn.

ara: +1. Also add a hard cap to avoid exploding for pathological sequences. We can expose flag --comm-pool-max=1.2G and --comm-pool-percentage=0.8 to tune.

kevin: I sketched a small patch to the allocator: allocate_comm_workspace(requested) -> rounded = min(requested, pool_max); try reuse from pool; if not available, fallback to async-alloc and record metric comm_pool_misses.

perf-bot: quick micro-benchmark (local emu)
```
baseline (no pool): avg allocs/sec=1200  comm_alloc_bytes=1.3G  OOMs=2
with pool (N=4, clamp=1.2G): avg allocs/sec=340  comm_alloc_bytes=0.48G  OOMs=0
```

dennis: Nice. Any perf hit on latency?

kevin: <1% p50 increase in end-to-end 95th for single-request latency on short-only batches. Long-batches stable. Throughput slightly better due to fewer stalls.

zach: About KV cache — can we switch to a shared KV region per-model per-node and have each TP shard point into offsets (no copy)? Might be tricky for sharded params but for KV it's just cache — should be doable if we change allocator to support sub-views that don't own memory.

maya: Implementation sketch: on decode start, create node-shared KV alloc (pinned per-NCCL-gang), populate full KV once, then on shard init assign views with stride and offset mapping. Add a flag --kv-shared=true behind FF.

ara: Danger: concurrency for writes (if any) and lifetime management across multiple requests. We need refcounting + eviction semantics. Also KMS/HSM customers may object to shared memory unless within same tenant. But for Dedicated it's fine.

kevin: Test plan I propose:
- small canary on dev pool with --comm-pool-max=1.2G N=4 + --kv-shared=true
- run chat-gen v12 for 4h with synthetic mix (mix ratio 80% short/20% long)
- gather metrics: per-rank peak mem, comm_pool_misses, latency p50/p95, output diffs for quality

dennis: Can add tracing hook to collect per-collective requested vs allocated sizes: TRACE:COMM_REQUEST(requested_bytes, allocated_bytes, reuse_hit)

zach: Also instrument batching heuristic: record max_nonpad_tokens per batch and see distribution to pick safe clamp.

maya: I'll prepare the CLA for pool allocator and a prototype for kv-shared view. Want to deploy to dev today.

kevin: Great — FYI I think this will also reduce staging fragmentation because fewer transient alloc/free cycles.

sre-bot: Started infra run: dev-pool/comm-pool-canary at 2039879900 UTC. Monitoring -> alerts on OOM > 0.

kevin: Thanks. If we get green on dev, we'll roll to staging and then canary on dedicated jobs.

ara: One last note: ensure we still support fallback to per-request runtime allocation for cross-tenant privacy in private deployments. Keep flags per-deployment.

kevin: Agreed. I'll open PR with design doc + perf numbers and link here when ready.

zach: Thanks all.
